newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak SAX falls 2.2 pts on Slovnaft losses.
newsitem.headline: Slovak SAX falls 2.2 pts on Slovnaft losses.

text.p: Slovak shares continued their downtrend in listless trading on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on Tuesday, with the 16-share SAX index pulled lower by losses to oil refiner Slovnaft.
Slovnaft closed down 49 crowns at 901 as the SAX eased 2.2 points to 181.77.

Brokers said the bourse still suffers from a lack of liquidity caused by a turbulence on the country's money market over the last month and the weak performance of a number of companies registered on the BSE.
Bourse officials, who presented the May trading preview on Tuesday, said even the listed companies were showing a downward trend.
"Only five (listed) companies paid or will pay a 1996 dividend at levels at least comparible with the previous year," General Secretary of the BSE Marian Sasik said.

Steel maker VSZ closed unchanged at 620 crowns after a 30-crown loss on Monday, but its average price, on which the SAX is being calculated, was lower by 1.4 percent. However, only 282 VZS shares traded.

Overall, volume fell to 356,518 shares, from 712,903 shares traded on Monday, while turnover decreased to 144.72 million crowns from 590.07 million. Both volume and turnover were boosted by direct trades.
